cards.label: Base housing
cards.q: Which ARX5 joint sweeps the azimuth, and what drives it?
cards.a: J1, the base yaw, driven by an EC-A4310 actuator inside the 59.9 × 60.0 × 62.5 mm base.

cards.label: Slot insert 11 × 3 × 2.7 mm
cards.q: What is the 11 × 3 × 2.7 mm insert beside each EC-A4310?
cards.a: Unconfirmed. ARX doesn't name it; its rounded-end shape suggests a key or a light guide.

cards.label: EC-A4310 rear housing (driver side)
cards.q: Which actuator drives ARX5 joints 1 to 3?
cards.a: The ENCOS EC-A4310-P2-36: Ø56 × 60.5 mm, 382 g, 36:1, 12 N·m rated, 36 N·m peak.

cards.label: EC-A4310 stator housing
cards.q: What surrounds the EC-A4310's stator?
cards.a: A finned middle housing, 29.5 × 55.9 × 56.0 mm, between the rear driver housing and the output ring.

cards.label: EC-A4310 output ring housing
cards.q: What clamps the EC-A4310's output ring to its stator housing?
cards.a: Six M3×16 socket-head cap screws, through 12 holes on the ring's rim.

cards.label: Actuator output hub
cards.q: What does the next ARX5 link bolt to?
cards.a: The EC-A4310's counterbored output hub, 12.0 × 34.9 × 35.0 mm.

cards.label: Encoder magnet cap
cards.q: What holds each EC-A4310's encoder magnet cap?
cards.a: Six M1.6×3 cap screws. The cap sits where the output-side magnetic encoder target is.

cards.label: M3×16 socket head cap screw
cards.q: How was this ARX screw identified, and how many are in the arm?
cards.a: Measured in ARX's CAD: head Ø5.5 × 3, shank Ø3 × 16 mm, ISO 4762 M3. 18 in all, six per EC-A4310.
cards.terms: CAD: computer-aided design · ISO: International Organization for Standardization

cards.label: M1.6×3 socket head cap screw
cards.q: What do the tiny M1.6×3 screws hold?
cards.a: Each EC-A4310's encoder magnet cap, six per cap and 18 in the arm; ISO 4762 M1.6.

cards.label: Ø2 × 4 dowel pin
cards.q: What are the three Ø2 × 4 mm pins in ARX's CAD?
cards.a: Plain dowel pins measured at Ø2.00 × 4.00 mm, one beside each EC-A4310 by position.

cards.label: M3 base mounting screw (from below)
cards.q: How can an ARX5 base be fixed down?
cards.a: Into four M3 tapped holes on a 46 × 46 mm square in its underside; ARX publishes no mounting procedure with these files.

cards.label: Motor core (simplified solid)
cards.q: How does ARX's CAD model the inside of the EC-A4310?
cards.a: As one plain 23.0 × 41.9 × 42.0 mm solid for stator and rotor; the internals shown beside it are estimates.

cards.label: Output bearing (Ø30.6 / Ø42 × 7 mm)
cards.q: What bearing does ARX's CAD show at each EC-A4310 output?
cards.a: A ring with a Ø30.6 bore, Ø42 outer diameter and 7 mm width: the envelope of a 61806 deep-groove bearing.

cards.label: Planetary ring gear
cards.q: What reductions do the ARX5's two actuator types use?
cards.a: 36:1 in the EC-A4310-P2-36 and 10:1 in the DM-J4310-2EC, both planetary.

cards.label: Planet gears (×3)
cards.q: Why are a planetary gearbox's small gears called planets?
cards.a: They orbit the central sun gear inside the ring gear, the way planets circle the Sun.

cards.label: Sun gear
cards.q: Where does motor torque enter a planetary gearbox?
cards.a: At the sun gear on the rotor shaft; the planets carry it out to the output.

cards.label: Stator (24 slots)
cards.q: What kind of motor sits inside each ARX5 actuator?
cards.a: A brushless DC motor. The DM-J4310 has 14 pole pairs, so 28 magnet poles on its rotor.
cards.root: stator ← Latin stāre, 'to stand': the part that stays still

cards.label: Stator windings
cards.q: What do the copper windings in an ARX5 actuator do?
cards.a: They carry the phase currents that build a rotating magnetic field; the rotor's magnets follow it round.
cards.root: copper ← Latin cuprum, from aes Cyprium, 'metal of Cyprus'

cards.label: Rotor with magnet ring
cards.q: How many magnet poles does a DM-J4310 rotor carry?
cards.a: 28. The datasheet lists 14 pole pairs, and each pair is one north and one south pole.
cards.root: magnet ← Greek magnētis lithos, 'stone of Magnesia'

cards.label: Encoder magnet (motor side)
cards.q: How does an ARX5 actuator sense its rotor angle?
cards.a: A diametric magnet on the shaft spins over a magnetic encoder chip that reads the field's direction.

cards.label: Driver + dual-encoder PCB
cards.q: Why can a DM-J4310 report its output angle right at power-on?
cards.a: Two 14-bit single-turn magnetic encoders give the output's absolute position; the driver talks CAN at 1 Mbps.

cards.label: Driver components
cards.q: Do the components on the ARX5 driver boards follow the real layout?
cards.a: No. The motor makers don't publish their boards, so these are representative.

cards.label: Yaw bracket body
cards.q: What is link 1 of the ARX5?
cards.a: The yaw bracket between J1 and J2; J1 swings it about the vertical axis. Its envelope is 57.5 × 59.4 × 72.5 mm.

cards.label: Yaw bracket cover plate
cards.q: What is the 6 mm plate on the ARX5's link 1?
cards.a: The yaw bracket's cover plate, 6.0 × 57.5 × 59.3 mm in ARX's CAD.

cards.label: ARX logo decal
cards.q: Why are some ARX5 surfaces paper-thin in the CAD?
cards.a: They're zero-thickness logo faces, merged here so each follows the shell it's printed on.

cards.label: Upper-arm shell, half B
cards.q: How is the ARX5 upper arm built?
cards.a: From two shells split lengthwise, half A and half B, each about 320 mm long; J2 to J3 is 264 mm.

cards.label: Upper-arm shell, half A
cards.q: How big is upper-arm shell half A?
cards.a: 30.3 × 56.0 × 319.8 mm in ARX's CAD; it pairs with half B to form link 2.

cards.label: Rear shaft cap
cards.q: What closes the rear of the J2 and J3 actuators?
cards.a: A plain rear shaft cap, 16 mm across and 5.0 mm thick.

cards.label: Forearm side plate
cards.q: What forms the ARX5 forearm?
cards.a: Two side plates, each 38.2 × 102.0 × 290.9 mm; J3 to J4 is 245 mm along the arm.

cards.label: Raised logo lettering (1 mm)
cards.q: How is the forearm's raised lettering modelled?
cards.a: As five separate solids, each 1 mm thick, in ARX's CAD.

cards.label: DM-J4310-2EC actuator
cards.q: Which actuator drives ARX5 joints 4 to 6, and how strong is it?
cards.a: The Damiao DM-J4310-2EC: Ø56 × 46 mm, 300 g, 10:1, 3 N·m rated, 7 N·m peak.

cards.label: Wrist-pitch motor cradle
cards.q: What is the 56.1 × 60.5 × 70.5 mm part on link 4?
cards.a: A cradle sized around a Ø56 DM-J4310 actuator at J4; the name comes from its shape, not from ARX.

cards.label: Wrist-pitch bracket
cards.q: What is the wrist-pitch bracket on the ARX5?
cards.a: Part of link 4, between J4 and J5, measured at 41.0 × 61.9 × 65.8 mm.

cards.label: Wrist-pitch cover plate
cards.q: What is the thin plate on the ARX5's link 4?
cards.a: A 5.0 mm cover plate, 31.0 × 54.3 mm, on the wrist-pitch link.

cards.label: Wrist-yaw housing
cards.q: Which ARX5 link carries two DM-J4310 actuators?
cards.a: Link 5, the wrist-yaw housing: it holds the J5 yaw and J6 roll actuators.

cards.label: Wrist cable connector block
cards.q: What is the 7.0 × 12.6 × 20.5 mm block on the wrist?
cards.a: A small block on link 5. Its role as a cable connector block is inferred from shape and position, not confirmed by ARX.

cards.label: Gripper base plate
cards.q: What carries the ARX5 gripper's rail and drive?
cards.a: The gripper base plate, 14.6 × 58.7 × 174.0 mm.

cards.label: MGN9 linear guide rail
cards.q: What do both ARX5 gripper fingers ride on?
cards.a: One MGN9-size rail, 9 mm wide, with a 20 × 28.9 mm carriage per finger.

cards.label: Gripper side bracket
cards.q: What is the curved 60 mm bracket on the gripper?
cards.a: A side bracket with a hole at each end, 10.0 × 25.0 × 60.0 mm; ARX doesn't describe its role.

cards.label: Pinion gear
cards.q: What sits between the two ARX5 finger racks?
cards.a: A spur pinion of about 12 teeth; turning it moves both racks equally in opposite directions.
cards.root: pinion ← French pignon, from Latin pinna, 'battlement'

cards.label: DM-J4310-2EC gripper actuator
cards.q: What motor drives the ARX5 gripper, and how hard can it squeeze?
cards.a: A DM-J4310-2EC. The SDK caps gripper torque at 1.5 N·m over its 88 mm width.

cards.label: Gripper motor mounting ring
cards.q: What seats the ARX5 gripper motor?
cards.a: A mounting ring with a hexagonal pocket, 11.0 × 57.0 × 57.0 mm.

cards.label: Hex output adapter
cards.q: What couples the gripper motor's output to the pinion?
cards.a: A hexagonal adapter with six holes, 11.7 × 34.6 × 37.0 mm.

cards.label: Gear rack
cards.q: How does one motor open both ARX5 fingers symmetrically?
cards.a: Each finger carries a gear rack; one central pinion meshes with both and drives them in opposite directions.

cards.label: Finger
cards.q: How far does each ARX5 finger travel?
cards.a: 0 to 44 mm per finger (X5A URDF); the SDK's gripper width is 88 mm.
cards.terms: URDF: Unified Robot Description Format · SDK: software development kit

cards.label: MGN9C carriage block
cards.q: What carries each ARX5 finger along the rail?
cards.a: An MGN9C carriage block, 20 mm wide and 28.9 mm long.
cards.root: carriage ← Old North French cariage, from carier, 'to carry'
